newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark scarred at US noon, Fed fears ebb on data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark scarred at US noon, Fed fears ebb on data.

text.p: Weak U.S. manufacturing data and subdued wage pressures eroded expectations of a near-term interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve, pushing the dollar lower versus the mark by midday, dealers said.
Dollar/yen, however, was unchanged and mark/yen gained after the dollar decline on the mark accelerated, as longs were liquidated and stop-loss selling kicked in under 1.7240.
"The market was caught long (dollar/mark) this morning," said Scott Duncan, a vice president at Credit Agricole. "The data was the catalyst that helped trigger some stops, no doubt about that."

The dollar got a toehold at 1.7220 marks in New York and changed hands at 1.7240/50 at midday, down from 1.7320/30 at the open. Although it briefly dipped to 126.59, dollar/yen stood unchanged from the open at 126.80/85.

The slide versus the mark was fueled by two numbers released at the U.S. open. The relatively tame 0.6 percent rise in the Labor Department's first quarter employment cost index came out side by side with a report showing durable goods orders tumbled 3.0 percent in March
Economists and traders said the data took some of the heat off the Fed to raise interest rates soon to slow the economy.

Economists polled by Reuters expected the durables data to be unchanged after a downwardly revised 0.8 percent rise in February. Wage costs, over which the Fed has recently expressed alarm, were expected to rise 0.9 percent.

"Everyone was speculating a higher employment cost index and obviously the bonds opened up a point and half higher. People trading interest rate differentials have to rethink the scenario now with the possibility of the Fed not hiking in May," said Russell LaScala chief dealer at Citibank.
While traders were exiting long positions, speculators reportedly weighed in with fresh short-sales of their own.
A weaker reading on consumer sentiment from the Conference Board also hung over the dollar during the morning. The confidence index fell to 116.8 in April from 118.5 in March.
The dollar's decline gathered momentum below Monday's low at 1.7250 marks. But the dollar steadied before it challenged important support at 1.7200/10.
But if this prop gives way, dealers said they expect a more vigorous decline to 1.7150 marks, and possibly "very key support" around 1.7085/90.
Meanwhile, the dollar shrugged off a huge rise in the Dow industrials. Traders said the Dow/dollar link broke ages ago.
"The connection between the Dow and the dollar, there was a decoupling there last summer. It's not a big factor," said Stephen Jury, chief dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.
Blue chip industrial shares were up more than 100 points at midday, in tandem with the soaring Treasury bond market, as investors rejoiced at diminished inflation prospects.

The market was barely fazed by afternoon remarks from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel. Waigel said the statement issued by the Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers in Washington on Sunday was meant to be stronger than their last message on currencies from Berlin in February.
In other trade, mark/yen jumped over 73.50 from early levels near 73.20. The mark was also firmer against the pound and some European currencies.
The dollar fell to 1.4655/65 Swiss francs from 1.4740/50 and to Canadian $1.3974/79 from C$1.4006/11. The pound rose to $1.6315/25 from $1.6218/28.
